reading.title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
reading.note: The best mental model for understanding why data needs context and why intuition often misleads us.

reading.title: The Visual Display of Quantitative Information
reading.note: Foundational for anyone who wants to communicate data clearly. Charts are arguments — make them honest ones.

reading.title: Shape Up
reading.note: A practical framework for scoping and shipping work without infinite backlogs. Applies beyond software teams.

reading.title: Everybody Lies
reading.note: What search data reveals that surveys never could. A reminder that the question you ask determines the answer you get.

tools.title: Pandas + Jupyter
tools.note: My primary stack for data cleaning, exploration, and analysis. Reproducible, versionable, and endlessly composable.

tools.title: Observable
tools.note: A notebook environment for data visualization in the browser. Great for shareable, interactive charts without a server.

tools.title: Tally
tools.note: The cleanest form builder I've found. No branding on the free tier, logic jumps, and integrations that actually work.

tools.title: Airtable
tools.note: Spreadsheet-database hybrid that works for small teams doing market research or content pipelines without a developer.

talks.title: The Beauty of Data Visualization
talks.note: A compelling case that good visualization is not decoration — it's a form of knowledge compression.

talks.title: How to Spot a Misleading Graph
talks.note: Short and essential. The ability to read charts critically is a core business literacy skill most people never develop.

talks.title: The Humane Representation of Thought
talks.source: Bret Victor · Media for Thinking the Unthinkable · 54 min
talks.note: A challenging and inspiring talk about how the tools we use shape what thoughts we can have. Relevant to anyone building with data.
